records.text: The first place that U.S. forces went during the Iraq War and set up a base was a museum that held relics, Babylonian cuneiform tablets, and Gilgamesh's tomb.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep QRS_hR7NXaQ)

appearances.snippet: The first place that we went during that war and set up a base was a museum. Not just any museum, the museum that held all of the relics. licks for that. It also held all the cuneiform tablets from Babylon and Gilgamesh and or Nimrod's tomb.

verification.notes: Transcript asserts that the museum/relic site was the first destination and base of U.S. forces. Current institutional records show Camp Alpha was established at Babylon after the invasion, but do not show it was the first place U.S. forces went; the Gilgamesh work was at Uruk, a different site. The composite claim is false.

sources.title: Report on Damage Assessments in Babylon
sources.relevance: UNESCO documents the later military base at Babylon but does not support the first-destination allegation.

sources.title: German Archaeological Institute - Uruk (Warka)
sources.relevance: Official project page locates the Gilgamesh-related prospecting at Uruk, not the Babylon museum/base.

records.text: U.S. forces set up Camp Alpha directly on ancient Babylon.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: You can look this up yourself that we, like I told you, set up our military base Camp Alpha right on top of ancient Babylon.

verification.notes: Transcript context matches the claim. UNESCO and British Museum documentation confirms coalition forces established Camp Alpha over roughly 150 hectares at the archaeological site of Babylon beginning in April 2003.

sources.title: Report on Damage Assessments in Babylon
sources.relevance: UNESCO confirms a military base was established across the ancient Babylon site beginning in April 2003.

records.text: A 2005 British Museum report said coalition forces' use of Babylon as a camp was tantamount to establishing a military camp around the Great Pyramid or Stonehenge.
records.speaker: British Museum

appearances.snippet: Now, according to a 2005 British Museum report, the use of Babylon as a camp by a multinational force between April 2003 and December of 2004, pardon, by coalition forces is, quote, tantamount to establishing a military camp around the Great Pyramid in Egypt or Stonehenge in Britain.

verification.notes: Transcript quotes the British Museum assessment. The museum's Babylon teaching resource reproduces the comparison that establishing a military camp at Babylon was equivalent to doing so around the Great Pyramid or Stonehenge, matching the substance of the statement.

sources.title: Babylon: Teachers' resources Key Stages 2 and 3
sources.relevance: British Museum resource reproduces the Great Pyramid and Stonehenge comparison.

records.text: Babylon was plundered during the 2003 war, and items from the Hammurabi and Nebuchadnezzar museums and the Babylon library and archive were stolen and destroyed.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Britain tells us later that Babylon was indeed plundered during the 2003 war when content from Hammurabi and Nebuchadnezzar museums and from the Babylon library and archive were stolen and destroyed.

verification.notes: Transcript context concerns post-invasion damage and looting at Babylon. Contemporary reporting based on the British Museum assessment states the Hammurabi and Nebuchadnezzar museums were broken into, contents stolen or smashed, and the library and archive destroyed, supporting the statement's substance.

sources.title: Attack on Ancient Babylon
sources.relevance: Contemporary AP/CBS account documents break-ins, theft and destruction at the museums, library, and archive.

records.text: A senior U.S. military officer was willing to apologize for damage his troops caused at one of Iraq's most famous ancient sites.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #2 (Ep QRS_hR7NXaQ)

appearances.snippet: It tells us that a senior U.S. military officer has said that he's willing to apologize for damage that his troops caused in one of Iraq's most famous ancient sites.

verification.notes: Transcript context matches contemporary reporting. A senior U.S. officer, Colonel John Coleman, publicly said he was willing to apologize for damage caused by military occupation of Babylon while disputing some allegations.

sources.title: US colonel offers Babylon apology
sources.relevance: Reports Colonel John Coleman saying he was willing to apologize for military damage at Babylon.

records.text: After the 2003 invasion, U.S. Marines built a helicopter pad on Babylon's ruins and filled sandbags with archaeological fragments.
records.speaker: BBC

appearances.snippet: The British Broadcasting Corp reported Friday that after the 2003 invasion of Iraq, U.S. Marines built a helicopter pad on the ruins of Babylon and filled their sandbags with archaeological fragments from the ancient city.

verification.notes: Transcript claims a helipad was built and archaeological material entered sandbags. The British Museum damage assessment and contemporaneous reporting document a helicopter landing area and sandbags/earthworks containing ancient pottery, brick, and other archaeological fragments.

sources.title: Report on Meeting at Babylon 11th-13th December 2004
sources.relevance: British Museum assessment documents the helicopter area and archaeological fragments in military works and sandbags.

conveyance.original_source: BBC report cited by NBC News

records.text: Vibrations from U.S. helicopters caused the roof of a building at Babylon to collapse.
records.speaker: BBC

appearances.snippet: It said vibrations from the U.S. helicopters caused the roof of one of the buildings to collapse. We were not there to protect.

verification.notes: Transcript claims helicopter vibration caused a roof collapse. Contemporary BBC reporting on the Babylon assessment records the allegation that helicopter movements caused vibrations leading to the collapse of a nearby temple roof; the statement accurately conveys the documented assessment.

sources.title: US colonel offers Babylon apology
sources.relevance: Contemporary report records the assessment that helicopter vibrations led to a nearby temple roof collapse.

conveyance.original_source: BBC report cited by NBC News

records.text: U.S. forces were at Babylon to plunder, loot, and steal, not to protect ancient ruins.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: We were not there to protect. Ancient ruins we were there to plunder and to loot and to steal.

verification.notes: Transcript context distinguishes alleged motive from documented damage. UNESCO and British Museum records establish serious damage and looting at Babylon, but current searches found no reliable evidence proving U.S. forces occupied the site with the purpose of stealing artifacts. Intent remains unverifiable.

records.text: Locals reported that Americans dug and extracted material at night in military operations at Babylon.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Locals reported that at night Americans were digging and they were extracting in military operations.

verification.notes: Transcript attributes nighttime digging and extraction to unnamed local reports. Current searches located institutional damage assessments but no reliable, traceable source establishing this specific eyewitness allegation. Verification attempted; the report cannot be substantiated.

records.text: The United States established 500 military bases and the world's largest embassy in Babylon after invading Iraq under false pretenses.
records.speaker: Rob Skiba

appearances.snippet: We all know we went into Iraq under false pretenses, right? They told us weapons of mass destruction, right? They said that we didn't find weapons of mass destruction, but I have a feeling we found the weapon of mass destruction and we set up shop there immediately after that and established 500 military bases in the largest embassy of any other embassy on the entire planet in Babylon.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. Government records support that the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad was described as the world largest, but it is in Baghdad rather than ancient Babylon. GAO counted 311 U.S. installations in May 2008 and 283 in November 2008, not 500; false pretenses is an evaluative characterization.

sources.title: Operation Iraqi Freedom: DOD Assessment of Iraqi Security Forces Units — GAO
sources.relevance: Reports 311 U.S. installations in May 2008, contradicting the 500-base figure.

sources.title: U.S. Senate Hearing on Embassy Security and Operations in Iraq
sources.relevance: Government hearing record describes the Baghdad embassy as the largest in the world.
